# TigerSetup 0.14.1

TigerSetup is a command-line tool for Windows that builds installers. Describe
your application in a `TigerSetup.toml`, and `tiger-setup build` produces one
self-contained `Setup.exe` with a wizard, a quiet mode for automation, upgrade,
repair and uninstall, and no runtime prerequisites on the target machine. The
installers it builds are transactional: an install or upgrade completes or rolls
back, and each installation records what it owns, so upgrade, uninstall and
verification work from what is really installed.

## What is new in 0.14.1

- **A successful uninstall leaves nothing behind.** Uninstalling — from
  Settings, with WinGet, or with `Setup.exe uninstall` — now also removes the
  uninstall's own log, the temporary copy of the uninstaller and its folder,
  the `TigerSetup` folder that held the installation's records once no other
  product's are left in it, and the empty `%TEMP%\TigerSetup` folder. An
  uninstall that fails keeps its log, and the outcome says where it is. This
  applies to TigerSetup itself and to every installer you build with it;
  rebuild with 0.14.1 to get it.
- **More robust installation records.** An installer now checks the folder it
  keeps an installation's records in before it writes anything there, and
  refuses one that is a link to somewhere else or that another account created
  and filled, rather than adopting it. For all-users installations the shared
  `%ProgramData%\TigerSetup` folder is now writable by administrators only.
  Records that belong to another product or scope are refused rather than
  used. Logs never overwrite a file through a link, and the installer engine
  checks that it reads the same `Setup.exe` file the loader started from.
- **Verified prerequisite downloads.** When an installer resolves a
  prerequisite from the WinGet catalog, it now checks the catalog's Microsoft
  signature and every hash from the catalog index down to the downloaded
  installer, as WinGet itself does, before running anything.
- **Licence and third-party notices.** TigerSetup now installs `LICENSE.txt`
  and `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` beside `tiger-setup.exe`, and the notices cover
  every third-party component in TigerSetup and in the installers it builds.
  `tiger-setup notices` and `Setup.exe notices` print them, so an installer you
  distribute carries the notices of the TigerSetup code inside it.
- **Privacy statement.** [`PRIVACY.md`](https://github.com/rkozlowski/TigerSetup/blob/main/PRIVACY.md)
  describes what TigerSetup records on your computer, what it removes, and the
  only network access it makes: downloading a prerequisite a package declares
  and the computer lacks, from the WinGet catalog or from the address the
  package names. TigerSetup sends no telemetry.
- **Version-specific WinGet links.** A `[winget]` URL in `TigerSetup.toml` may
  write `{version}` where the package version goes, so a licence or release
  notes link names the release the manifests are for:

  ```toml
  [winget]
  license_url = "https://github.com/example/myapp/blob/v{version}/LICENSE"
  ```

  TigerSetup's own WinGet metadata now names its repository, issues, release
  notes, licence and privacy statement.

## Install

Download `TigerSetup-0.14.1-Setup.exe` below and run it. It installs per user
by default (no administrator rights needed) or for everyone on request, and
adds `tiger-setup` to `PATH` unless you clear that option. For scripts:

```text
TigerSetup-0.14.1-Setup.exe install --quiet
TigerSetup-0.14.1-Setup.exe install --quiet --scope machine
```

TigerSetup runs on Windows 10 1809 or later, Windows 11 and Windows Server 2019
or later, x64.

## Verify the download

`SHA256SUMS.txt` lists the SHA-256 of the installer and of its WinGet manifest
set, and `release-artifacts.json` records the same hashes with the commit they
were built from; all four files come from one build of that commit, and the
release's tag names that record's own SHA-256. The installer and the programs it
installs are not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen may ask before running
the installer.
`tiger-setup inspect TigerSetup-0.14.1-Setup.exe` decodes and checks any
TigerSetup installer without running it.
